clue.text: Out of class, suffering heart flutter

indicators.note: the word's heart, its middle pair of letters, flutters and changes places, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: a form is a school class

explanation.surface: A pupil off school because of palpitations.
explanation.walkthrough: Only the two middle letters swap; the outer letters stay put.
explanation.definitionFit: As a preposition, 'from' marks origin or source, just as 'out of' does in 'made out of wood'.

clue.text: Poetry about a painter

indicators.note: the poetry word goes around, about, the other piece

parts.note: verse is poetry
a, as in a single one

explanation.surface: A poem written about some artist.
explanation.walkthrough: Paolo Veronese was the 16th-century Venetian painter, named after his birthplace, Verona, which also ties to the puzzle's Two Gentlemen theme.
explanation.definitionFit: Veronese is the name by which the Renaissance artist Paolo Caliari is known.

clue.text: See 8
Looking up 109kg messenger, one of 18 13 down 29 26 across

definitions.note: the cross-reference spells THE WINOS FORD VIEWS, which decodes to The Merry Wives of Windsor

indicators.note: in a down entry, looking up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: printed with its superscript lost: 10 to the power 9 kilograms is a million million grams, a teragram
a page is a boy employed to run messages

explanation.surface: A messenger glancing up under an enormous weight.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue meant 10⁹ kg; the superscript went missing in print. 'THE WINOS FORD VIEWS' becomes The Merry Wives of Windsor by taking 'Merry' as an anagram signal: WINOS FORD VIEWS rearranges to WIVES OF WINDSOR.
explanation.definitionFit: Mistress Margaret Page is one of the two wives who outwit Falstaff in Shakespeare's comedy.

clue.text: Worn out, but lively when cycling

indicators.note: cycling moves the front part of the word round to the back

parts.note: upbeat means cheerful and lively

explanation.surface: A tired person who perks up on a bike ride.
explanation.definitionFit: Something beat-up is battered and shabby from long use, i.e. worn out.

clue.text: The Elephants, Blue Horses etc, being ordered in 2s for ark

indicators.note: the letters are put into a new order

parts.note: animals entered the ark in twos
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Elephants and horses lining up two by two to board Noah's ark.
explanation.walkthrough: The Elephants is a Dalí painting and Blue Horses one by Franz Marc; the surface wants them to be animals queueing for the ark.
explanation.definitionFit: Both titles are famous paintings, examples of artistic creations.

clue.text: The Rock of Marseille in connection with south of quay

indicators.note: in a down entry, what is south of something sits below it, so it comes after

parts.note: a pier is a landing stage like a quay
re means concerning, in connection with

explanation.surface: A rock beside the harbour in the French port of Marseille.
explanation.walkthrough: Pierre is French for stone or rock, and the name Peter means rock too.
explanation.definitionFit: In French, the language of Marseille, the everyday word for a stone or rock is pierre.

clue.text: Fit, I agree

definitions.meaning: second meaning: an expression of assent, as in 'oh, all right'

explanation.walkthrough: Read together the words sound like one person consenting to something; they are two separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase describes someone in excellent health and is also a reply granting consent.

clue.text: Turn over realm's second most prominent magistrate

indicators.note: turned over, so the word for turn is read backwards

parts.note: veer means change direction

indicators.note: only the second letter of the word realm is used

parts.note: the word realm, of which only its second letter is taken

explanation.surface: A kingdom's top judge gets overturned.
explanation.definitionFit: Historically a reeve was the chief officer or magistrate of a town or district.

clue.text: A letter describing numbers having entered compound

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: describing in the geometric sense of drawing round, so one piece goes around the other

parts.note: dee is the spelt-out name of the letter D
in, as in arrived or entered

explanation.surface: A letter explaining figures that have been entered in some walled area.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Describing' is the geometry sense, to trace a line around something.
explanation.definitionFit: Adenosine is a chemical compound, a nucleoside built from adenine and ribose.

clue.text: Perform other work, a piece for piano

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to take a second job, often on the quiet

explanation.walkthrough: Beethoven's Piano Sonata No 14 is popularly known as the Moonlight Sonata.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means to work a second job besides one's main one, and the noun names a famous sonata.

clue.text: A piece of Ireland bishop's kept in locker

indicators.note: one piece is kept inside the other

parts.note: a key is what locks
RR, Right Reverend, is a bishop's title; the 's is 'is'

explanation.surface: A bishop stashes a relic from Ireland in his locker.
explanation.walkthrough: Right Reverend is the formal style of an Anglican bishop. Kerry is a county in the south-west of Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: County Kerry is one region of the island, a part of Ireland.

clue.text: Keeping time, women playing there who will give you the edge?

definitions.text: who will give you the edge?

indicators.note: the rest of the letters keep, hold, the time piece inside
playing means the word there is rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Women keep time while making music somewhere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Edge' is a sharp blade, not an advantage.
explanation.definitionFit: A whetter sharpens tools, giving a blade its keen cutting edge.

clue.text: Prevail over 8 big drinkers

indicators.note: in a down entry, the first piece sits over the second

parts.note: to win is to prevail
8 down's first word is very, and very big is outsize, OS

explanation.surface: Beating some heavy drinkers.
explanation.walkthrough: '8' stands for VERY, the first word of 8 down. OS is the clothing-size label for outsize.
explanation.definitionFit: Winos are alcoholics, people who drink cheap wine heavily.

clue.text: Their fathers naval officers? Changing times!

definitions.meaning: first meaning: sons of men of the sea
second meaning: spring, summer, autumn and winter, which change through the year

explanation.walkthrough: Split the second word in two and the answer becomes children of seafarers.
explanation.definitionFit: The four seasons are the periods into which the year divides as it turns.

clue.text: With roll of fat for one of 27 2 23

definitions.note: 27, 2 and 23 give A COUPLE OF VERONESE SWELLS: Two Gentlemen of Verona

parts.note: pro means in favour of, with

indicators.note: rolling the word over reads it backwards

parts.note: suet is hard animal fat

explanation.surface: Something with a roll of fat, offered for a character.
explanation.walkthrough: The cross-reference reads 'a couple of' (two), 'Veronese' (of Verona), 'swells' (gentlemen).
explanation.definitionFit: Proteus is the fickle friend of Valentine in Shakespeare's The Two Gentlemen of Verona.

clue.text: Deal with mounting problem for drivers on a course?

indicators.note: in a down entry, mounting means climbing, so the letters run upwards

parts.words: problem for drivers on a course
parts.note: O TEES, zero tees, would trouble golfers wanting to drive off

explanation.surface: Handling a growing difficulty for golfers on the links.
explanation.walkthrough: Drivers are golf clubs; having no (O) tees to drive from is the golfer's problem.
explanation.definitionFit: To see to a task is to attend to or handle it.

clue.text: A bit short of power for new member of the family

indicators.note: the piece is short of, lacking, the letter for power
a replacement comes in for what was lost

parts.note: a piece is a bit

explanation.surface: A slightly underpowered newcomer joining a family.
explanation.definitionFit: A niece, a sibling's daughter, is a relative, someone belonging to the family.

clue.text: As endlessly inspired by hearties in resort?

definitions.text: As endlessly inspired by hearties in resort?

indicators.note: inspired by means breathed in by, so the shortened word goes inside the rearranged letters
resort read as re-sort, sorting the letters again into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: endlessly means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: taken as written, minus its last letter

explanation.surface: Hearty holidaymakers at a seaside resort breathe something in, a kind of riddle about what that is.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Resort' does double duty: re-sort for the anagram, and the seaside town where the hearties breathe deep. The whole clue then describes the answer, an &lit.
explanation.definitionFit: Bracing sea air is what hearty types gulp down at a coastal holiday town.

clue.text: American in love? Dear me, no — how awful

indicators.note: an exclamation of dismay, signalling the letters are thrown into disorder

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone horrified at the idea of a Yank falling in love.
explanation.walkthrough: 'American' points to the US spelling without the U.
explanation.definitionFit: Enamored is the US spelling of enamoured, meaning smitten or captivated.

clue.text: One of 18 13 down 29 26 across coal-fired fans

definitions.note: THE WINOS FORD VIEWS, with merry as an anagram signal, decodes to The Merry Wives of Windsor

indicators.note: fans out, spreads the letters into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Fans in a coal-fired power station.
explanation.walkthrough: 18, 13 down, 29 and 26 across read THE WINOS FORD VIEWS; 'merry' as anagram signal turns WINOS FORD VIEWS into WIVES OF WINDSOR.
explanation.definitionFit: Mistress Alice Ford is one of the two scheming wives in Shakespeare's comedy The Merry Wives of Windsor.

clue.text: In an emergency, belting female's jumping in bed with earls

indicators.note: belting means wrapping round, so the jumbled letters enclose the female piece
jumping signals the letters leap into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
E is an abbreviation for earl, so two earls give two of them

explanation.surface: An emergency: a woman leaping into bed beside some aristocrats.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is 'is' joining the parts.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means 'if necessary', used of a step taken only should the need arise.

clue.text: Mum missing let me think these females could be from flighty mistress

indicators.note: fickle and changeable, so the remaining letters are rearranged
taken from, removed out of the word mistress

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: Mum missing the hesitation sound leaves just its first letter

parts.note: taken as written
um is the sound of hesitation while thinking

explanation.surface: Without Mum, could these girls be the offspring of a fickle mistress?
explanation.walkthrough: Mum minus UM leaves M; that M comes out of mistress before the shuffle.
explanation.definitionFit: Sisters are female siblings, so women in a family related to one another.

clue.text: See 27 across
See 18 across
7's 24 1 8 5 17 after 18, one hundred and ten?

definitions.note: PIERRE'S SEA AIR FROM VERY BEAT-UP NIECE after THE gives THE MERCHANT OF VENICE

parts.note: an means one
a ton is a hundred
IO looks like the digits 10

explanation.surface: A numbers puzzle summing to a hundred and ten.
explanation.walkthrough: Pierre's sea air is French MER CHANT (sea song); FROM gives OF; VERY gives V and BEAT-UP shuffles NIECE: V + ENICE = VENICE.
explanation.definitionFit: Antonio is the merchant in Shakespeare's The Merchant of Venice, the play's title character.

clue.text: What climbers seek to contend with, rivals holding hands?

parts.note: to vie is to contend or compete
West and South are opponents at bridge, each holding a hand of cards

explanation.surface: Mountaineers grappling with difficulties, competitors gripping hands.
explanation.walkthrough: In bridge North-South play East-West, so W and S sit on opposing sides.
explanation.definitionFit: Mountaineers often climb for the panorama from the top, the vistas they hope to see.

clue.text: 65, or 54? (OAP's essential verbal test)

indicators.note: the essential, central part of the word, only its middle letter

parts.note: an OAP is an old-age pensioner; its middle letter is the one kept

explanation.surface: A pensioner's age and a spoken assessment.
explanation.walkthrough: The same letters split two ways give both numbers. A viva is strictly an oral exam, so 'verbal' means spoken here.
explanation.definitionFit: A viva voce is an oral examination, as for a doctorate, where candidates answer spoken questions.

clue.text: Song from Fred and Judy too, extra piece of brilliance by Delibes — fine soprano

indicators.note: the extra items are packed inside the phrase for too

parts.note: as well means too
a coup is a brilliant stroke
Léo Delibes, the French composer

explanation.surface: Astaire and Garland's number, plus a dazzling soprano encore from Delibes.
explanation.walkthrough: Fred Astaire and Judy Garland sang it in Easter Parade (1948).
explanation.definitionFit: The number is a duet the pair performed as tramps in the musical film Easter Parade.

clue.text: See 4
See 20 across

parts.note: the answer runs unbroken through these words, from the middle of prevalent across in into the start of Eden

clue.text: What Blarney Stone and Midas give an actress?

King Midas turned what he touched to gold, or in heraldry
